neighbours.label: ' of' right after 'out' (came out of nowhere, hit it out of the park, the way out of …); weaker on other fixed-phrase slots ('the best one can say')
fire: A grey cat appeared out of nowhere and ran across the road.
The idea seemed to come out of thin air during the meeting.
Her speech at the wedding was completely out of the blue.
The singer hit it out of the park on opening night.
He pulled the answer out of nowhere at the last second.
The only way out of this mess is to tell the truth.
A loud bang came out of the darkness behind the barn.
The rumour grew out of nothing more than a careless remark.
quiet: A grey cat appeared on the wall and ran across the road.
The idea seemed to arrive suddenly during the meeting.
Her speech at the wedding was a complete surprise.
The singer was a great success on opening night.
He gave the answer to the judges at the last second.
The price of this mess is a week of extra work.
A loud bang came from the darkness behind the barn.
The rumour was the result of a careless remark.

notes: Card: ' of' is 10 of the top 32 peaks, mostly after 'out'. Probe: 'out of nowhere' 1.06, 'out of the park' 0.39, 'the most one can say' 0.65; two plain sentences reached 0.33-0.34, so near misses may leak.
